finding: The claim error table has the rows "fetch refused by the remote" and "push refused for another reason". The seed error table has one row, "access refused by the remote". A seed that a pre-receive hook refuses is a refused push, not a refused access, so a reader cannot tell which seed row covers it. All three rows name the same message, the remote and git's error message, so only the wording differs. Fix: Use one name per case in both tables. For example, rename the seed row to "push refused by the remote", if a seed only pushes. Add a "fetch refused by the remote" row only if a seed also reads the remote.
why_this_severity: The seed error table says `access refused by the remote`, where the claim table says `fetch refused` and `push refused`, so a reader cannot tell which seed row covers a hook refusal. All three rows print the same message, so an implementer can act (no to fails_purpose). No code encodes the row names.
